warnings.message: Topic has no hard prerequisites and is not marked foundational.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Copy repeating patterns
node.description: Copy simple repeating patterns using objects, sounds, movements or symbols.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Extend repeating patterns
node.description: Continue repeating patterns by identifying what comes next.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Identify repeating pattern unit
node.description: Identify the smallest repeating unit that generates a repeating pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Create repeating patterns
node.description: Create repeating patterns with a chosen repeating unit and describe the rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Translate repeating patterns
node.description: Represent the same repeating pattern using different materials, symbols or actions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growing pattern terms
node.description: Identify terms in a growing pattern and describe how each term changes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Extend growing patterns
node.description: Continue growing patterns by applying their change structure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Describe growth rule in words
node.description: Describe how a growing pattern changes from term to term using everyday and mathematical language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Represent growing patterns with diagrams
node.description: Use diagrams or materials to represent and analyse growing patterns.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growing pattern tables
node.description: Organise term numbers and term values of a growing pattern in a table.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Additive number patterns
node.description: Recognise and extend number patterns generated by adding or subtracting a constant amount.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiplicative number patterns
node.description: Recognise and extend number patterns generated by multiplying or dividing by a constant factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Skip counting patterns
node.description: Connect skip counting sequences to additive number patterns and multiples.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Input output pattern tables
node.description: Use input-output tables to represent pattern rules connecting term numbers and values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Near and far pattern terms
node.description: Find near and far terms of a pattern using structural reasoning rather than repeated extension only.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Word rules for patterns
node.description: Write word rules that describe how to find any term of a pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Symbolic rules for patterns
node.description: Use variables and symbols to write general rules for patterns.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent pattern rules
node.description: Recognise when different rules produce the same pattern values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Linear pattern rules
node.description: Recognise and write linear rules for patterns with constant first differences.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Patterns to graphs
node.description: Represent pattern relationships as ordered pairs and simple graphs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Recursive versus explicit rules
node.description: Distinguish rules that give the next term from rules that give any term directly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Pattern unit repeats
node.description: A repeating pattern is generated by repeating the same unit in order.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Position matters in patterns
node.description: The position of an item or term matters when describing and predicting a pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growing pattern changes by structure
node.description: A growing pattern changes in a structured way from one term to the next.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tables show term and position
node.description: A pattern table can connect each term number with its term value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant difference suggests linear rule
node.description: A constant first difference suggests an additive or linear pattern rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiplicative pattern uses factor
node.description: A multiplicative pattern changes by multiplying or dividing by a constant factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: General rule finds any term
node.description: A general rule can find any term of a pattern without listing every previous term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variable can represent term number
node.description: A variable can represent the term number when writing a general pattern rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent rules give same outputs
node.description: Equivalent pattern rules produce the same output values for the same inputs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Explicit rule uses position
node.description: An explicit rule uses the term position to calculate the term value directly.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Pattern unit too large
node.description: Learner identifies a repeated segment that contains more than one full repeat of the smallest pattern unit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Extend by last item only
node.description: Learner predicts the next item based only on the last item rather than the pattern unit or structure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growing pattern treated as repeating
node.description: Learner treats a growing pattern as if it repeats unchanged rather than increasing or changing structurally.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rule only describes next step
node.description: Learner gives a recursive next-step description when the task requires a rule for any term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Use term value as position
node.description: Learner confuses the term number with the term value when using a table or rule.

edge.rationale: Copying repeating patterns is an early repeating-pattern skill.
Extending repeating patterns directly practises recognising the repeating structure.
The repeating unit is the core structure of a repeating pattern.
Creating repeating patterns practises applying a chosen pattern unit.
Translating a pattern across representations practises structural recognition.
Identifying terms is foundational for growing-pattern analysis.
Extending growing patterns practises recognising growth structure.
Describing growth in words supports early generalisation.
Diagrams are core representations for growing patterns.
Tables organise term positions and values for growing patterns.
Additive number patterns are central number-pattern cases.
Multiplicative number patterns extend additive patterns into factor-based change.
Skip counting is an early additive number-pattern form.
Input-output tables support generalising pattern rules.
Finding far terms encourages general rather than recursive reasoning.
Word rules are a core form of early pattern generalisation.
Symbolic rules are a central algebraic generalisation outcome.
Equivalent rules deepen understanding of generalised pattern structure.
Linear pattern rules are a common major target of generalising rules.
Graphing pattern relationships connects rules to coordinate representations.
Distinguishing recursive and explicit rules clarifies types of pattern generalisation.
Copying object patterns uses early matching and sequencing skills, though it can also develop alongside them.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not preserve one-to-one correspondence between model and copy.

edge.rationale: Extending a repeating pattern depends on first reproducing and tracking its sequence.
edge.failure_signal: Learner copies items but cannot determine the next item.

edge.rationale: Identifying the repeating unit builds from extending the repeated sequence.
edge.failure_signal: Learner names several repeats instead of the smallest repeating unit.

edge.rationale: Creating a repeating pattern requires choosing and repeating a unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner makes a sequence that changes unpredictably instead of repeating.

edge.rationale: Translating a pattern across representations requires preserving the repeating unit structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes the structure when switching materials or symbols.

edge.rationale: Growing pattern work builds on recognising ordered pattern terms and structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the sequence of terms in a visual pattern.

edge.rationale: Extending a growing pattern requires identifying its terms and how they change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner repeats a previous term instead of extending the growth.

edge.rationale: Describing growth builds on seeing how the pattern extends term by term.
edge.failure_signal: Learner can draw the next term but cannot describe the change.

edge.rationale: Diagram representations require identifying the term structure of a growing pattern.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws disconnected pictures rather than structured terms.

edge.rationale: Tables organise described growth by term number and term value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner lists term values but does not connect them to positions.

edge.rationale: Additive number patterns build on repeated addition or counting-on reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify a constant additive change.

edge.rationale: Multiplicative number patterns depend on multiplication and division relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats multiplicative change as repeated addition only when a factor is needed.

edge.rationale: Skip-counting patterns build on counting on from a starting number.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot keep a constant skip size through the sequence.

edge.rationale: Input-output pattern tables extend growing-pattern tables into rule-based relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses term number and term value columns.

edge.rationale: Finding near and far terms uses term-number and term-value structure from tables.
edge.failure_signal: Learner extends one term at a time for far terms instead of using structure.

edge.rationale: Word rules emerge from reasoning about how any term is found, not only the next term.
edge.failure_signal: Learner states only 'add three' when an any-term rule is required.

edge.rationale: Symbolic pattern rules require variable notation for term number or input value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot use a variable to represent a changing term position.

edge.rationale: Recognising equivalent pattern rules requires interpreting symbolic rules as producing values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sees different-looking expressions as unrelated without checking outputs.

edge.rationale: Linear pattern rules build on additive patterns with constant difference.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes a rule that matches early terms but fails later terms.

edge.rationale: Graphing patterns requires representing term-position and value pairs as ordered pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots term values without using term numbers as inputs.

edge.rationale: Distinguishing recursive and explicit rules requires interpreting different forms of pattern descriptions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot tell whether a rule gives the next term or any term directly.
